<thought>From the spectrum, the most distinctive pattern is the M+2 peak (213 m/z) that is about one‑third the intensity of the monoisotopic peak (211 m/z). This 3:1 ratio is characteristic of a single chlorine atom (35Cl/37Cl). No other element shows a clear, unique isotopic signature (e.g., bromine would give an M+2 peak of roughly equal intensity, which is not observed). Therefore, chlorine is the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution.</thought>
<final_answer>['Cl']</final_answer>
